description_clean: Chi siamoNailscamp è un'azienda e-commerce innovativa specializzata nella cosmesi professionale per unghie. la conoscenza del tedesco o del francese costituisce un plus.Orientamento al cliente e alla community: Passione per l'interazione con le persone, attitudine all'aiuto e pazienza nel gestire le richieste dei clienti.Gusto creativo ed estetico: Forte senso per l'armonia visiva, l'estetica moderna del settore beauty, i trend attuali e la tipografia.Disponibilità e impegno: Capacità di integrare agevolmente nella propria routine un orario di lavoro di 40 ore settimanali, nella sede di Berlino.Affinità con il mondo dei cosmetici: Un'esperienza pratica o un forte interesse per le unghie in gel, lo smalto o la nail art rappresentano un grande vantaggio (saremo felici di insegnarti tutte le nozioni tecniche sul prodotto).Prima esperienza: Precedenti stage o esperienze pratiche nel social media marketing, nell'influencer outreach o nel servizio clienti costituiscono un plus.Cosa offriamoSocial & Marketing al centro: I nostri canali digitali sono fondamentali per la crescita del brand — il tuo lavoro avrà un impatto immediato e visibile sul mercato italiano.Rapido percorso di apprendimento: Un ambiente dinamico e agile in cui potrai prendere l'iniziativa, testare le tue idee ed ampliare rapidamente le tue competenze.Ambiente collaborativo: Un team affiatato e disponibile che ti supporterà durante l'onboarding e in ogni fase della tua crescita professionale.Base solida da cui partire: Accesso all'esperienza e agli asset di account aziendali già avviati, con un seguito combinato di oltre 160.000 follower su Instagram e TikTok.Ambiente di lavoro moderno: Stipendio competitivo, orari di lavoro flessibili, sconti per i dipendenti e attrezzatura di lavoro moderna.Prospettive a lungo termine: Chiare opportunità di avanzamento di carriera e di inserimento a tempo indeterminato.Come candidarsiTi sembra il ruolo giusto per te? title: Talent Acquisition Specialist - Operations & Supply Chain (m(w/d)
description_clean:
Unser Kunde ist ein etabliertes Unternehmen im Bereich Fracht- und Lagerlösungen und optimiert Prozesse rund um Warentransport und -verteilung.
Als Operations Recruiter gestalten Sie aktiv mit, wie ein Unternehmen wächst – denn ohne die richtigen Menschen an Bord bleibt jede Wachstumsstrategie nur Theorie. Sie sind die Schnittstelle zwischen Fachbereichen und Talenten, verstehen die operativen Herausforderungen im Detail und finden genau die Persönlichkeiten, die diesen Bereich voranbringen. Kein Recruiting von der Stange, sondern echtes Verständnis für Prozesse, Teams und Menschen.
Wenn Sie gern eigenverantwortlich arbeiten, ein Gespür für Menschen haben und dabei sein wollen, wenn Teams entstehen, die den Unterschied machen – dann ist diese Rolle genau richtig für Sie.
Aufgaben

Mit klarem Fokus auf gewerbliche Mitarbeitende übernehmen Sie die Steuerung und Verantwortung für den gesamten Recruiting-Prozess bis zur erfolgreichen Besetzung.
In enger Kooperation mit der Agentur für Arbeit planen und leiten Sie Bewerbertage sowie Auswahlverfahren vor Ort.
Sie sprechen potenzielle Kandidaten proaktiv über verschiedene Kanäle an und pflegen die Bewerberdatenbank.
Zur effizienten Vorqualifizierung und Auswahl geeigneter Bewerber – sowohl gewerblich als auch kaufmännisch – organisieren und führen Sie strukturierte Interviews.
Mit internen Stakeholdern, Personaldienstleistern sowie dem Employer-Branding-Team stehen Sie in enger Zusammenarbeit.
Um einen reibungslosen und skalierbaren Projektaufbau sicherzustellen, analysieren Sie Recruiting-Kennzahlen und optimieren die Prozesse fortlaufend.

Qualifikation

Ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Betriebswirtschaftslehre (BWL), der Wirtschaftswissenschaften, der Wirtschaftspsychologie oder eine vergleichbare kaufmännische Ausbildung bringen Sie mit.
Sie verfügen über fundierte Erfahrung im Recruiting.
Idealerweise bringen Sie zudem Kenntnisse des regionalen Arbeitsmarkts in der Supply Chain mit.
Kommunikationsstärke und Organisationstalent zeichnen Sie ebenso aus wie eine strukturierte, eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise.
Sprachlich überzeugen Sie mit sehr guten Deutsch- sowie guten Englischkenntnissen in Wort und Schrift.

title: Consultant SAP S/4HANA Transformation
description_clean: Für viele Unternehmen ist S/4HANA ein Pflicht-Upgrade. Bei UNITY ist es deine Mission, daraus eine echte unternehmerische Entscheidung für unsere Kunden zu machen: Wohin soll sich die Prozess- und Systemlandschaft bewegen? Was kostet welcher Weg und wer setzt ihn um? Und wie bleibt das Programm steuerbar? Du sitzt auf der Seite des Kunden. Du gestaltest End-to-End-Prozesse, Zielarchitektur und Programmsteuerung. Die technische Implementierung übernimmt unser Partnernetzwerk.Unser Anspruch als Business Integrator: Wir schützen das, was unsere Kunden vom Wettbewerb unterscheidet (wir nennen das „Prozess-DNA“) und helfen ihnen zu verstehen, was sich nicht unterscheiden sollte.Das erwartet dichTransformationspfad entwickeln: Du arbeitest gemeinsam mit unseren Kunden und Team an Vorprojekten zur Auswahl von ERP-Systemen samt Definition von Zielbild, Leitplanken, Zielarchitektur, Deploymentvariante (RISE vs. GROW, Cloud vs. On-Premise) und Transformationspfad (Greenfield, Brownfield, Lift-&-Shift) inklusive Business Case.Zielarchitektur mitgestalten: Du arbeitest an Clean-Core-Konzepten, an SAP Business AI Platform (BAIP) – auf Basis von SAP BTP als Entkopplungsplattform und an Datenstrategien, etwa für Datasphere oder SAP Analytics Cloud.Programme transparent begleiten: Du unterstützt bei der Erstellung einer tragfähigen Roadmap und sorgst im PMO mit Tools wie SAP Signavio, LeanIX und SAP Cloud ALM für Klarheit über Fortschritt, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten.Den richtigen Partner an Bord holen: Du gestaltest Transformationsausschreibungen – im Mittelstand und Konzern ebenso wie vergaberechtskonform bei öffentlichen Auftraggebern und Kliniken.KI dort einsetzen, wo sie wirkt: Du identifizierst Use Cases for SAP Business AI und Joule, etwa in der Custom-Code-Analyse, bei der Datenqualität oder mit unseren KI-Agents in Einkauf, Supply Chain und Order-to-Cash.Branchenwissen aufbauen: Du arbeitest in Industrie und Handel, im Krankenhaus (IS-H-Ablösung, KIS-Szenarien) oder in der Energiewirtschaft (IS-U).Künstliche Intelligenz @UNITYBei UNITY arbeitest du mit KI, die du selbst mitgestalten kannst: die eigenentwickelte UNITY X-Plattform gibt dir Zugriff auf verschiedene Claude-, ChatGPT & Gemini Modelle. Copilot und Claude-Modelle sind direkt in Teams und den Microsoft-Anwendungen verfügbar. In Copilot Studio kannst du außerdem eigene Agenten bauen, wenn du willst. UNITY Coding Communities, Hackathons, AI Labs und das AI Trainings Camp geben dir Raum, eigene Lösungen für intern und für Kunden zu bauen.Das bringst du mitMust-haves JuniorErste Praxiserfahrung entweder in einer Management- oder IT-Beratung oder auf Kundenseite in der IndustrieVerständnis für Geschäftsprozesse in mindestens einem Bereich, zum Beispiel Finance, Logistik, Einkauf, Produktion oder Vertrieb, und Freude daran, diese zu analysieren und zu optimierenGrundkenntnisse der SAP-Vorgehensmodelle, etwa SAP Activate, und der MigrationsszenarienDie Fähigkeit, KI wirksam und sicher anzuwenden.Prägnante Kommunikation und Präsentation auf Deutsch (C1) und Englisch (mindestens B2)Ein abgeschlossenes Studium der (Wirtschafts-)Informatik, des Wirtschaftsingenieurwesens, der Produktionstechnik oder ein vergleichbarer Abschluss mit technischem oder betriebswirtschaftlichem SchwerpunktIdealerweiseErste Erfahrungen aus SAP-S/4HANA-ProjektenErste Berührungspunkte mit SAP BTP, Signavio oder LeanIXBranchenerfahrung in Industrie, Healthcare oder Energie(Senior Level): Entwicklung Architektur-Roadmaps rund um Clean Core und BTP.(Senior Level): Übernahme von Teilprojektleitungen oder Streamleadfunktion.Senior Level: Das bringst du zusätzlich mitDu hast bereits mindestens eine S/4HANA-Transformation über mehrere Phasen begleitet.Du bist an der Steuerung von Implementierungspartnern beteiligt gewesen und hast Scope-Entscheidungen mit dem Management deiner Kunden mitgetroffen.Du hast Erfahrung in der Sammlung und Darstellung von Use Cases und/oder Change-Requests im Kontext von SAP S/4HANA Transformations-Programmen.Juniors coachst du im Projekt, und du bringst eigene Ideen in unser SAP-Leistungsangebot ein.Ehrlich gesagt: Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn du vor allem selbst customizen oder in ABAP entwickeln willst. Die Implementierung liegt bei unseren Partnern, deine Stärke liegt im Steuern, Gestalten und Entscheiden. Sie passt auch nicht, wenn du lieber ein Modul tief betreust, als den Blick über Prozesse, Daten und Organisation hinweg zu weiten. Wenn dich dagegen die Frage reizt, wie aus einem ERP-Projekt messbarer Business-Nutzen wird, dann bist du bei uns richtig.Deine Chancen und MöglichkeitenProjekte mit Substanz: Du begleitest Transformationsprogramme von der Strategie bis zum Go-Live, in Industrie, Healthcare und Energie, und siehst, wie aus einem ERP-Projekt Business-Nutzen wird.Fachlicher Austausch auf Augenhöhe: Du arbeitest mit den Köpfen hinter unserem SAP-Angebot, darunter unsere Heads of SAP Architecture & Innovation und SAP Transformation Excellence.Partnernetzwerk statt Einzelkämpfertum: Du steuerst gemeinsam mit Implementierungspartnern, statt alles selbst zu bauen, und lernst dabei die gesamte Wertschöpfungskette einer Transformation kennen.SAP-Innovation aus erster Hand: Mit unserem zentralen KI-Team, AI Labs und Hackathons entwickelst du Business-AI-Use-Cases für den SAP-Kontext mit.Entwicklung vom Junior zum Senior: Deine SAP-Laufbahn ist bei uns kein Zufall, sondern ein Pfad bis zur Projektleitung und Architekturverantwortung. description_clean:

The ideal blend of stability and flexibility. A genuinely human employer that cares for people and the planet. True autonomy to shape what comes next, for us and you. This is the perfect platform to take your career where you want.

Over 200 colleagues of 47 nationalities. We’re the grown-up start-up, helping to shape a better future since day one.That hasn’t changed, even if the world has. We’re friendly, international, inclusive – and our people say we’re reliable and transparent, too. It’s why they trust us and believe in what we do.

Make Zattoo the TV platform partner of choice for operators and broadcasters in Eastern and Northern Europe. This role turns new markets into lasting revenue and shapes Zattoo’s next stage of growth. You will join a close-knit team working across Germany and Switzerland that values trust, collaboration and hands-on ownership over hierarchy and heavy process.  
THE TEAM
The Zattoo Business Sales Team is responsible for all sales activities related to Zattoo’s TV-as-a-Service and streaming technology offerings, including the End-to-End TV platform as well as Modular products such as Streaming, Ingest and Orchestration solutions. We work closely with Product, Portfolio Management, Marketing, Client Success and Project Management to bring complex solutions to market and build long-term customer relationships across different regions and customer segments.
WHAT YOU’LL DO

Build a new business pipeline across Eastern and Northern Europe and win telcos, ISPs, broadcasters and OTT platforms as long-term customers
Own complex, high-value deals end-to-end, from first conversation to signed contract
Navigate long decision cycles and orchestrate our Sales Engineering, Product and Legal teams to get deals over the line
Build lasting relationships with senior decision makers up to C-level
Shape tailored offers from our modular platform (INGEST, STREAM, ORCHESTRATE, E2E)
Be Zattoo’s face in your markets, at customer meetings, trade shows and partner events, and bring market insights back to Product

WHAT YOU’LL BRING
Experience required (Must-have)

10+ years in B2B enterprise sales, closing complex deals with long sales cycles
Proven track record selling to telcos, broadcasters, media companies or platform providers
Deep understanding of the TV, OTT and streaming market
Established network in Eastern and/or Northern European markets
Confident negotiating with C-level and procurement teams
Business fluent English

Nice to have

Language skills in one or more Eastern or Northern European languages
Experience selling modular tech or SaaS platforms
German language skills are advantageous

Behavioural Competencies

Ownership: Takes full responsibility for their markets and deals, without relying on a large sales support machine.
Honest Forecasting: Reports pipeline and forecast realistically and transparently, including bad news early.
Team Player: Works closely with Product, Sales Engineering and Legal and values collaboration over individual heroics.
Hands-on Mentality: Comfortable building structures and materials themselves where needed.
Long-term Thinking: Builds relationships for the long run instead of chasing quick wins.

WHY JOIN US? 
At Zattoo, you’re always on firm ground with real freedom to explore. You’ll have the support and opportunity you need to go far, while you’re helping us create a sustainable and entertainment-filled future for all.

Reward: strong market competitive salary
Recharge: 30 days vacation plus public holidays
Regulate: trust based flexible working hours and the option for remote work worldwide for up to 8 weeks per year

Plus:

We’re inclusive: ‘Zattooies’ are a fun, engaged, and diverse team made up of 47 nationalities
We’re healthy: Health checks, mental wellbeing support, team sports and more!

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
description_clean: What Quadrants isQuadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.The roleYou own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime.What you’ll ownAPI & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches.IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality.Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform.Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking.Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. title: Genesis-World: Core Physics Engineer
description_clean: What we're buildingRobots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future.Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI. One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available (paper). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact (paper) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise.Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.This is at the core of Genesis AI's strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.The roleYou push the physics of Genesis-World forward. The mandate is clear: ship production-ready simulation capabilities that matter for the company's internal needs. Research applied end-to-end, from algorithm to merged, tested, documented code that real robot-learning pipelines depend on. Occasional groundbreaking research happens, notably through academic collaborations. But the core of the job is making the engine measurably better along five axes:Speed. Algorithms that are not only faster but also smart enough to spend compute only where it matters across both time and space: larger stable timesteps, selective fidelity (adaptive across scales or simply hand-set), structure-aware solvers.Completeness. No physics off limits: water, human animation, air flow, gravel, tendons, even body organs. Whatever the next use-case needs, the engine grows to cover it.Fidelity. More realistic models: contact, friction, deformation, energy, actuation, materials…Versatility. Extensible multi-physics without compromise on realism: all solvers in the scene coupled together at once, two-way and constraint-based. Write your own solver and it joins the scene like a native one, growing into an open solver ecosystem.Scalability. From workstation to factory scale, and one day, city scale: thousands of interacting entities, batched across environments, without losing physical soundness.Our ambition is to establish Genesis-World as the go-to simulator for physical AI, from companies and research labs to individuals.The problems waiting for youEvery fidelity for every physics. Simulate at full fidelity what agents interact with and see, coarsely what they do not.Heterogeneous environments. Every parallel world can hold a completely different model: different bodies, joints, and collision geometries.Adaptive timesteps per island. Error-based control with Runge-Kutta Dopri5, and Time-of-Impact stepping during collision detection, as done in Jiminy.Couple everything, exactly. Efficient and accurate two-way constraint-based coupling between heterogeneous grey-box solvers, using state-of-the-art methods like ADMM. Owning every solver in the stack is what makes it possible.More scalable constraint solvers. Push rigid constraint solving beyond its current scalability ceiling (reference).Unify contact resolution. Hydro-elastic compliance, unilateral constraints, and sequential impulses in the same framework, ideally under one generic formulation.Closed kinematic loops without constraints. title: Genesis-World: Core Simulation Engine Engineer
description_clean: What we’re buildingRobots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future.Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI. One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available (paper). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact (paper) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise.Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.This is at the core of Genesis AI’s strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.The roleSimulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally.Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you.You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture.The problems waiting for youMake testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams.Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically.Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid.Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant.Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on.Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine.Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly.Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins.Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay.Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption.Who you areYou care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. Nous nous appuyons pour cela sur :L'automatisation par l'IA pour simplifier la gestion de la paie et le suivi réglementaire : c'est dans la transformation des usages métiers que l'IA a le plus de potentiel, et le marché de la paie et du social, largement ignoré depuis plus d'une décennie, est un terrain d'innovation immense.Une plateforme collaborative et ouverte, connectée à l'ensemble des outils métiers des cabinets, qui fluidifie les échanges entre les gestionnaires de paie et leurs clients.Une gestion avancée des données pour offrir à plus long terme un conseil social à 360° sur l'ensemble des problématiques paie et social : budgétisation de la masse salariale, construction intelligente des grilles salariales, gestion contractuelle avancée, avantages salariés, mutuelle, etc.L'objectif : développer le « Pennylane de la paie », une plateforme centrale de gestion paie et social pour les cabinets comptables et leurs clients TPE/PME.Chez Alassio, tu t'attaqueras à un défi de taille, qui te permettra d'évoluer comme nulle part ailleurs :Construire un logiciel particulièrement complexe, par son volet réglementaire, mais surtout par ses logiques profondes, qui doivent permettre de gérer la paie de façon exhaustive. C'est un logiciel métier dense, avec un impact immédiat sur la vie de ses utilisateurs (des dizaines de milliers de gestionnaires de paie, des centaines de milliers d'entreprises clientes), sur une fonction parmi les plus sensibles pour les TPE/PME françaises.Faire partie d'une équipe Tech resserrée, où chacun porte un ou plusieurs de nos chantiers techniques structurants et pose les fondations de notre plateforme métier. Nos Founding Engineers ont vocation à évoluer à terme vers des responsabilités de direction, selon leur appétence pour le management. 💻 Stack techniqueUne stack efficace et robuste, adaptée pour construire un logiciel métier et livrer des fonctionnalités à un rythme industriel.Full stack : Django / PythonBase de données : PostgreSQLInfrastructure et déploiement : Railway, GitHub Actions  Profil recherché 🌱 ExpérienceIndispensable :Excellente intuition produitGrande curiosité et esprit entrepreneurialIntérêt marqué pour les secteurs à forte composante métierGourou des dernières technologies d'IAUne vraie passion pour la techAu moins 3 ans d'expérience dans une entreprise tech de premier planUn plus :Maîtrise de Python / DjangoExpérience dans une structure à forte composante métier ou réglementaire (par exemple Pennylane, Alan, Qonto)Projets tech entrepreneuriaux ou personnelsExpérience en infrastructure et cloud 💎 QualitésGrande curiosité et capacité d'adaptationRage de vaincreProactivité  Processus de sélectionAppel d'introduction avec Tancrède (CEO) : 30 minEntretien technique avec Paul et Ayoub (CTO) : 1 hEntretien technique avec Ivan et Laura (Founding SWE) : 45 minRencontre informelle avec toute l'équipeEntretien d'adéquation culturelle avec deux de nos partenaires : 45 min👉 Le processus se termine par 3 prises de référence.  Ce que nous offrons 👊 Une mission uniqueChez Alassio, notre ambition est de remplir une mission que beaucoup présentent comme impossible techniquement, et de la remplir rapidement.Chez nous, il n'y a pas de place (et surtout pas le temps) pour des process inutiles ou des lourdeurs managériales : toute l'équipe est pleinement concentrée sur une mission claire, construire rapidement un outil tech exceptionnel.Tout est pensé en interne pour favoriser la vélocité technique : chez Alassio, les problématiques managériales ne remplaceront jamais les problématiques techniques et intellectuelles. Nous faisons le choix d'une équipe resserrée au départ, car l'histoire du marché montre qu'une petite équipe peut produire plus, mieux et plus vite que des géants. 💸 RémunérationNous valorisons un engagement à la hauteur des ambitions d'Alassio et proposons une rémunération supérieure aux standards du marché : 60 à 85 K€ de salaire fixe. title: Product Frontend Engineer
description_clean:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app.
quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.
Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.
The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.  
Where this is going
Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.
That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.
One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.
Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled.  
Why this role exists
Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.
What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.
That is the opening.  
How we work
We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.
We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.
And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.
Tasks
What you will own
Everything on the screen:

The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.
The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.
The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.
Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.
The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.

Where design ends, engineering begins.
We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.
Requirements
Who we are looking for
You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.
You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.
You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.
You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.
Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.
The Team
We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.
This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

ABOUT INSIFY
We sell a mix of insurance products to small businesses (SME's) in the Netherlands, Germany and France, and we are in the process of scaling into more markets. 
Insurance infrastructure is brutal to get right. Every carrier has its own spec, every product its own underwriting rules, every country its own regulatory requirements. Most insurers throw people and process at that complexity - one-off integrations, workarounds on workarounds. We're building it differently: our insurance platform is where we consolidate that complexity, so that launching a new product or market becomes a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild.
Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by more than €40M from investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.
About the role
You would join the Shop team, responsible for everything that happens after a small business buys a policy from us. You would help shape how the platform handles the next product and the next country, on a system already carrying live policies and real customers.
The team owns end-to-end policy lifecycle management (mid-term adjustments, automated renewals, cancellations, and payment flows) alongside the backoffice tooling that gives our operations and support teams full visibility and control. We work closely with the Claims Team, and with the Activation Teams that turn a lead into a paying customer. Product and engineering together are 30+ people.
Every country has its own regulatory quirks, and every insurance product has unique data structures, lifecycle rules, and money flows.
As we expand across Europe, our goal isn't to write custom glue code for every new launch. It's to design elegant, reusable platform abstractions. We're building a system where introducing a new country or product feels like snapping modular building blocks together.
You're joining at an exciting inflection point: we have real traction, proven scale, and you get to directly build the foundational platform that powers our next wave of European growth.
What you'll be doing
Owning end-to-end the discovery and delivery of crucial platform features that enable our ability to scale as an insurance business
Continuously and relentlessly seeking opportunities to turn new product demands into platform capabilities and features that scale across countries and insurance product lines
Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others
What you'll need
3+ years building complex web applications and services, with real production ownership
Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your direct stack to get to results, be that data / backend / frontend
You get real leverage out of AI in your daily work, and you can say where it helped, and where it hurt
Strong fundamentals in domain-driven design & service oriented architecture

Experience building B2B products, especially in insurance & fintech

Strong observability instincts. You know where things will break, and can help others learn that too

TypeScript across the board, running on AWS (IaaC), in a single monorepo. If you have not worked with all of it, that is fine. We care more about how you reason about systems than about which tools you have used before.

title: System Performance Intern
description_clean: About Pangea Propulsion:We are a company dedicated to developing advanced propulsion systems for the space industry based on three key principles: high efficiency, sustainability, and reusability. During this six-month internship, you will support system-level design, modelling and performance analysis activities for Kronos full-flow staged-combustion rocket engines.You will work closely with System Performance engineers and specialists in combustion, fluidics, turbomachinery and other disciplines to connect engine requirements and design choices with cycle modelling, subsystem characteristics and overall engine performance. You will be involved in the development and execution of engine models, investigating nominal, throttled and off-nominal operating conditions, and assessing how evolving subsystem designs influence the complete propulsion system. The work will include sensitivity studies, design trade-offs and support to the definition of operating and control strategies.This internship requires strong fundamentals in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, an understanding of liquid rocket-engine cycles, and the ability to interpret numerical results critically rather than treating simulation tools as black boxes. You will contribute to transient analyses covering start-up, throttling and shutdown, and consolidate results into engineering conclusions, performance maps, operating envelopes, subsystem requirements and technical documentation for design reviews.Key Responsibilities:· Develop, modify and execute system-level engine models in EcosimPro/ESPSS.· Analyse nominal operating points and engine operational envelopes, including throttled and off-nominal conditions.· Support engine-cycle optimisation and system-level design trade-offs.· Perform sensitivity studies on key design and operational parameters.· Translate simulation results into engineering conclusions, performance maps, operating envelopes and subsystem requirements.· Support preparation and maintenance of System Performance documentation for project design reviews.· Work with combustion, fluidics, turbomachinery and other disciplines to integrate evolving subsystem designs into the system model.What you need to be successful:· MSc in Aerospace Engineering or equivalent, preferably with a background in propulsion, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, energy systems or numerical modelling.· Experience with numerical modelling and engineering analysis through academic or professional projects.· Strong fundamentals in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and heat transfer.· Understanding of liquid rocket propulsion and the fundamental operation of rocket-engine cycles.· Ability to analyse coupled engineering systems and critically interpret simulation results.· Basic programming or engineering scripting capability, preferably Python and/or MATLAB.Soft Skills:· Strong analytical problem-solving skills.· Ability to communicate technical results clearly in English through documentation and presentations.· You are expected to work in a structured and analytical manner, communicate your results clearly, and progressively take ownership of defined modelling and analysis tasks while receiving guidance from experienced engineers.Other useful skills:· Experience with EcosimPro/ESPSS or another 0D/1D system-simulation environment.· Knowledge of staged-combustion or full-flow staged-combustion rocket-engine cycles.· Understanding of turbopumps, turbines, pre-burners, combustion chambers, regenerative cooling circuits, valves and feed systems.· Experience with transient simulation, controls or system dynamics.· Experience with sensitivity analysis, uncertainty propagation or Monte Carlo methods.· Experience processing engineering data using Python or MATLAB.· Familiarity with Git/version control and structured engineering-development processes.· A university project, thesis or previous internship involving propulsion-system modelling.Not hitting every Rigorous Experimental DesignControlled Comparisons & AblationsNearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). min)  🎁 Ce que l’on peut t'offrir :🏥 Une mutuelle parmi les meilleures sur le marché (Alan Blue et Alan Mind)🍜 Des tickets restaurants (Carte Swile)🏝 Entre 6 et 12 jours de RTT supplémentaires aux 5 title: Senior AI Specialist (Operations) (x/f/m)
description_clean: Doctolib is looking for you to join us as a Senior AI Specialist (x/f/m) at our Berlin location, starting as soon as possible.Doctolib is becoming an AI-native company. We are redesigning the way we work, workflow by workflow, and are looking for people who will not only support this transformation, but actively build it. As a Senior AI Specialist, you will be the technical builder and AI Ops Owner behind AI-powered productivity for our Operations and Customer Success teams. You will work in founder and product mode: you will own a workflow end to end, from context and agent design to evaluation, and continuously take it to a higher level of automation. Our ambition is to move away from manual case-by-case work towards workflows that run largely autonomously while maintaining a high quality bar. In this way, you will contribute directly to our mission of improving healthcare for everyone.Your ResponsibilitiesRedesign workflows rather than simply automating them: You analyze the most critical Operations and Customer Success workflows, break down time-consuming processes that require limited judgment, and transform them through the use of AI agents. You set clear objectives for autonomy and quality, and continuously develop them further.Build and operate AI agents as products: You develop and manage agents on platforms such as Dust or Claude. Each agent is deployed to production with a defined baseline and relevant metrics such as benefit, usage, and scalability.Knowledge and context management: You deliberately curate the context agents need, from templates to core data. The guiding principle is quality over quantity. You ensure that knowledge sources in Confluence, Drive, or Salesforce are always up to date and well structured.Evaluation and quality assurance: You define quality standards and establish evaluation routines to identify and address weaknesses such as hallucinations or prompt drift at an early stage. You continuously optimize prompts through systematic user feedback and A/B testing.CRM and data integration: You own the interfaces between CRM systems such as Salesforce and our AI platforms. You automate data flows and work closely with IT to unlock new, valuable data sources for our agents.Central interface and enablement: You translate business requirements into technical solutions and bring together stakeholders from Leadership, IT, and Product. You strengthen the team’s AI fluency in the areas of context, agent management, and evaluation.Impact and measurement: Rather than inventing new KPIs, you make the success of AI measurable using existing metrics such as time, quality, and cost, and use these insights to guide the next steps in scaling.Your ProfileSince production-ready AI workflows and agent technologies are still relatively new, years of market experience are rare. We therefore deliberately prioritize potential over years of experience alone. What matters to us is your ability to learn quickly, your strong product mindset, and your judgment. If you are passionate about this field and bring the necessary skills, we would be delighted to hear from you, even if your profile does not perfectly cover every single aspect.What Really Matters to Us, Regardless of the Specific Tool:Learning speed and a production mindset: You have taught yourself a new technical field from scratch and built something real that people actually used. You can describe precisely what went wrong, such as hallucinations, prompt drift, outdated data, or costs, and how you solved it.An instinct for evaluation: You do not rely on something merely “looking good”. You define a quality bar and measure against it. For you, automation and quality go hand in hand.Ownership and communication: You take ownership of a problem end to end, prioritize rigorously, feel comfortable with ambiguity, and make technical topics understandable to non-technical stakeholders.Technical and data understanding: You can read and adapt scripts, understand APIs, webhooks, and automation tools such as Make, n8n, and Zapier, and know how CRM data, ideally Salesforce data, flows into AI systems.Strong communication skills: You have a confident command of English and can operate at the highest level in our international environment. German at B1 level is sufficient.We Are Particularly Interested in:Expertise with agent platforms: You have practical experience with systems such as Dust, Claude, or LangChain. Since tools evolve quickly, we primarily rely on your process understanding and evaluation skills as a sustainable foundation.Technical depth and data fluency: You are proficient in languages such as Python or JavaScript and can confidently navigate Salesforce architectures or BI environments such as Tableau and Metabase to manage data flows effectively.Operations experience: You have solid experience working with scaled Customer Success or Operations teams and understand their specific dynamics.What We OfferA Germany-wide public transport pass sponsored by Doctolib if you work from the office or in hybrid modeCompany-sponsored health insurance with excellent additional benefits28 days of paid vacation, plus one additional day for every full calendar year of employment, up to a maximum of 30 daysParticipation in Doctolib’s long-term employee equity program, DoctoGrowthThe opportunity to work from abroad for up to 10 days per yearAn occupational pension scheme with an employer contribution of 40%, or 15% during the probationary periodThe Doctolib Parent Care Program, which includes one additional month of parental leave and much moreFree mental health and coaching sessions through an external partnerIn addition to healthy snacks and a regular breakfast buffet, we offer meal vouchersA subsidized sports program with our partner Urban Sports ClubFor caregivers and employees with disabilities, we offer support that includes more flexible working hours, additional leave for medical reasons, and psychological supportThe Interview ProcessInterview with TalentHiring Manager interviewOn-site case studyFinal interview with VPReference checksOfferJob DetailsPermanent positionFull-timeLocation: BerlinStart date: JulyHybrid, 2 days working from home per weekOur vision is to improve the health of everyone. title: Senior Product Designer
description_clean: In just over two years, we’ve gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We have a big mission: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run and grow a renewables installation business – and through that to make a massive dent in the world’s carbon emissions and create a hugely better experience for homeowners.We’re now looking for a stellar Product Designer who’s buzzing to create exceptional experiences for installers as we expand into new markets.🌲 About SpruceAlmost 20% of the UK’s carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there’s simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can’t currently offer a heat pump when someone’s boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.We’re fixing this. We’ve built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we’re having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and have been scaling the team to massively grow our impact. We’re in the process of expanding outside heat pumps and by the end of the year will be an operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and autoCAD, you might get a sense of where we’re headed…🥖 The RoleYou’ll be central to our mission as we turn historically slow and painful processes into ones that are quick, intuitive and even delightful for installers. We’ve been design-led since the beginning but the challenge is only growing as our product becomes (necessarily) more complex. Day-to-day you’ll be:Making complex decisions feel effortless – Our platform handles everything from building physics calculations to fluid dynamics modelling to complicated compliance requirements. We need to make handling that complexity feel effortless for all our customers, irrespective of how tech-savvy they are.Designing across multiple touchpoints – You'll work on desktop design tools, homeowner-facing outputs, enquiry flows, mobile survey apps (incl LiDAR), and collaborative workflows that work seamlessly across different user types (from 3-person local installers to national utilities);Collaborating closely with developers & shipping code yourself – Understanding data structures and technical constraints so your designs can be shipped quickly; and shipping PRs yourself when it makes sense (with the support of the dev team);Building systematic, scalable design systems – Creating robust, structured, and reusable components that work across platforms and for potentially low-tech users;Researching and validating - Interviewing and spending time with installers to deeply understand how they work and what the core problems to solve are; and building quick prototypes to test and validate design decisions and uncover unexpected pain points.You'll report directly to Steph, our Co-Founder and CPO.🫵 About YouWe’re looking for a designer with 3+ years of product/UI design experience (and potentially a lot more), ideally in a startup context or within fast-paced, impact-focussed teams. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone altogether every fortnight.You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is clearly particularly important for this role but you’ll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers.We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. title: Research and Development Engineer in Artificial Intelligence - 12 months contract
description_clean: Who we are ?Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools.The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment.Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing potential attacks, understanding the strategies available to attackers and defenders, and verifying that critical security properties are preserved. Formal verification provides rigorous methods for addressing these challenges, allowing engineers to reason about system behaviours and establish mathematical guarantees. However, applying these techniques to realistic systems remains challenging. Verification problems can involve large state spaces and complex strategic interactions, while constructing formal models and specifying security properties often requires specialised expertise.The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges by combining formal verification with artificial intelligence. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for analysing cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. The project also investigates how AI can improve the efficiency and accessibility of these verification processes.A central objective of VITAMIN-C is to integrate AI techniques into the verification workflow. On the computational side, AI models will be investigated to guide the exploration of large state spaces and prioritise promising verification strategies. By learning from previously verified models and their associated results, these components can help identify relevant search directions and reduce the computational effort required by verification algorithms. On the usability side, the project explores AI-assisted interfaces that support engineers in constructing formal models and specifying security properties. These interfaces may exploit natural-language processing and large language models to interpret engineering descriptions, suggest formal representations, and assist users throughout the verification process. In both cases, the correctness of verification results remains the responsibility of the underlying formal methods, which validate the outcomes produced or suggested by AI components.Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of AI techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on developing AI components for verification guidance, investigating natural-language and LLM-based assistance for formal modelling, and integrating these capabilities into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in the preparation of training and evaluation datasets, the development of experimental benchmarks, and the assessment of the proposed approaches in terms of effectiveness, computational efficiency, and reliability. The overall objective is to make formal verification more scalable and accessible while preserving the rigorous guarantees provided by the verification framework.Your main responsibilities will include :Carry out R&D work in artificial intelligence for formal verificationContribute to the research profile of Télécom Paris and Institut Mines-Télécom  The candidate must have a solid understanding of artificial intelligence, Python programming, data processing and analysis, and software engineering. title: Chief Customer Officer
description_clean:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 
Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank. We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.
Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job. We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow. We are committed to changing the way things are done.
Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position Work from anywhere!Position overview
Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 
Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.
The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.
The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.
This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.
The mandate

 Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
 Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would. You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
 Win the right members, efficiently. You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
 Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances. Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
 Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless. You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
 Build one Customer organisation, not four. Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
 Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call. You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate
This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.

title: Design System Manager - Consultant.e
description_clean:
Mindset
Chez Thiga, nous considérons qu’un Design System n’est pas seulement un ensemble de composants ou de règles : c’est un produit à part entière. Un produit pensé pour évoluer, répondre aux besoins des équipes, et accompagner la croissance de l’entreprise.
Créer et faire vivre un Design System demande une vision, une stratégie claire, et une gouvernance solide. Il faut piloter son adoption, anticiper ses usages à grande échelle, et s’assurer qu’il réponde aux enjeux à la fois du Design et de la Tech. C’est un levier puissant pour faire monter en maturité les organisations, structurer la collaboration entre les équipes, et diffuser une culture produit forte.
Aujourd'hui, un Design System bien structuré est aussi la condition sine qua non pour tirerpleinement parti de l'IA dans les workflows design et prototypage. Tokens cohérents,composants documentés, nomenclature rigoureuse autant de fondations qui permettentd'exploiter les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Lovable, v0...) de manière fiable et scalable.Le.la Design System Manager de demain est celui.celle qui anticipe ces usages et structure son système en conséquence.
Les Design System Managers que nous recherchons pensent leur système comme un produitvivant, automatisé au maximum, et conçu pour connecter Design et Ingénierie dans un workflowsans friction.How we work together 🤝
Mettre en place des rituels d'adoption et d'amélioration continue :offices hours, sessions de feedback, contribution guidelines pour que le DS soit co-construit et adopté par toutes les équipes.
Aligner Design et Engineering en continu : organiser des syncs réguliers avec les équipes dev pour garantir la cohérence entre les composants Figma et leur implémentation code. Le DS ne vit pas dans Figma seul; il vit dans la production.
Piloter l'alignement stratégique multi-équipes : s'assurer que Produit, Tech, Design et business partagent la même vision et roadmap du DS, intégrée au même niveau que les autres produits.
Répondre aux besoins des utilisateurs et contributeurs : centraliser les demandes, prioriser les évolutions, et faciliter la contribution fluide de designers, développeurs et PMs.
Fédérer autour d'une culture DS partagée : faire du DS un produit vivant et co-créé, en favorisant des échanges transparents et en embarquant les équipes dans sa vision long terme
How we get work done 🚀
Définir et piloter la roadmap du DS : feuille de route alignée sur les priorités produit et business, avec des objectifs mesurables à court et long terme.
Automatiser les workflows du DS au maximum : pipelines de tokens, synchronisation design to code en temps réel, scripts de génération de documentation, réduire au minimum les tâches manuelles et les risques de désynchronisation.
Structurer le DS pour l'IA et le prototypage rapide : concevoir une architecture de composants et de tokens qui rende le DS exploitable par les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Cursor, v0, Lovable...). Cela implique : nomenclature stricte,variantes bien définies, props documentées, et une logique de composants qui s'aligne avec les patterns du code.
Garantir la cohérence design-code : mettre en place des outils de vérification automatique pour s'assurer que ce qui est designé est bien ce qui est développé sans avoir à le vérifier manuellement.
Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques à grande échelle : formations, ateliers, documentation vivante pour que le DS soit utilisé de manière fluide et scalable par toutes les équipes.
Mesurer l'impact et itérer : KPIs d'adoption, indicateurs de qualité, retours qualitatifs pour évaluer l'impact du DS et ajuster les priorités
How our work creates impact 🎯
 Accélérer le delivery produit : composants prêts à l'emploi, pipelines automatisés et prompts IA calibrés sur le DS. Les équipes conçoivent et développent plus vite, avec moins de friction
Rendre le prototypage IA fiable et scalable : un DS bien structuré devient le langage commun entre les designers et les outils d'IA les prototypes générés sont cohérents avec la prod, pas jetables
Garantir la qualité et la cohérence design à l'échelle : expérience utilisateur homogène, identité de marque renforcée, dette design et technique réduite
Réduire la dette et simplifier la maintenance : moins de doublons, moins de variantes inutiles, un code plus accessible et plus performant
Faire monter l'organisation en maturité design : culture de collaboration Design × Tech structurée, vision stratégique du design renforcée, documentation vivante comme levier de montée en compétence
Compétences 💼
Vision système et stratégie DS : u sais définir une stratégie de DS et la décliner en roadmap concrète, en alignement avec les priorités produit, tech et business. Tu fais preuve de leadership pour porter cette vision et embarquer les équipes.
Alignement Design-Engineering : tu as une solide compréhension des enjeux front-end (tokens, design-to-code, systèmes de composants) et tu dialogues en égal avec les développeurs pas seulement pour les convaincre, mais pour co-construire les bonnes solutions.
Automatisation et tooling DS : tu maîtrises les pipelines de tokens, les outils de documentation (Storybook, Zeroheight) et tu as une appétence pour l'automatisation des workflows DS.
IA et prototypage avancé : tu comprends comment un DS structuré permet de tirer parti des outils d'IA générative pour le design et le prototypage. Tu anticipes ces usages dans les décisions d'architecture du DS.
Gestion de produit interne : tu pilotes le DS comme un vrai produit : besoins utilisateurs, priorisation, KPIs, itération continue.
Communication et influence : tu sais formuler des livrables synthétiques et stratégiques (vision, roadmap, modèles de gouvernance, dashboards) pour aligner des interlocuteurs variés équipes opérationnelles, direction produit, stakeholders.
Outils : figma (Variables, Dev Mode, Make), Storybook, Zeroheight, Notion, Jira/Linear, Style Dictionary, et une bonne aisance avec les environnements no-code/low-code et outils IA de prototypage.

description_clean: Mines Saint-Etienne est une Ecole de l’Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT), 1er groupe public d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management en France. L’IMT est un EPSCP (grand établissement) sous la tutelle du Ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique.L’École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Saint-Étienne (Mines Saint-Etienne) est chargée de missions de formation, de recherche et d’innovation, de transfert vers l’industrie et de culture scientifique, technique et industrielle.Mines Saint-Etienne représente: 2 400 élèves-ingénieurs et chercheurs en formation, 480 personnels (150 Chercheurs et Enseignants-chercheurs), un budget consolidé de 46 M€, 3 campus dédiés à l’industrie à Saint-Etienne et Lyon (région AURA), à la microélectronique et aux objets connectés à Gardanne (Métropole Aix-Marseille Provence, région SUD) et à l’ingénierie pour la santé à Saint-Etienne ; 6 unités de recherche ; 5 centres de formation et de recherche ; un centre de culture scientifique technique et industrielle leader en France « La Rotonde » (> 50 000 visiteurs / an). Contexte scientifique et objectifs du stage :Des dispositifs d’électronique organique ultra-flexibles, conformables et implantables incorporant une intelligence artificielle promettent de révolutionner la surveillance et le traitement en temps réel de maladies chroniques [1]. De tels systèmes pourraient être basés sur des transistors organiques électrochimiques (OECTs), exploitant des conducteurs polymères mixtes ion-électron (PMIECs) comme couches actives. En effet, les PMIECs sont apparus comme une excellente plateforme matérielle pour interfacer la biologie avec l’électronique conventionnelle ; identifié comme le domaine de la « bioélectronique organique ou plastique ». L’OECT est considéré comme l’éléments clé pour réaliser une telle interface [2]. Son efficacité est évaluée suivant des figures de mérite (FoMs) telles que i) la transconductance (gm), et/ou ii) les temps de commutation (ionique vs. électronique) dans le dispositif. Au-delà des applications de transduction, à court terme, l’OECT est aussi intéressant pour créer des applications émergentes en matière de circuits neuromorphiques bioélectroniques [3].La réalisation de tels circuits est freinée par un manque de compréhension et d’optimisation des processus de conduction mixte dans ces matériaux polymériques ; notamment une asymétrie des temps de commutation des transistors lors des séquences de dopage (i.e « ON ») vs dédopage (i.e « OFF ») dans le canal de l’OECT. Des outils de caractérisation in-situ & operando permettant de quantifier et cartographier les paramètres de transduction électronique et électrochimique dans le canal de l’OECT se révèlent être indispensables pour comprendre les limitations actuelles en performances des PMIECs et/ou pour construire des PMIECs optimums dans de tels circuits neuromorphiques. Dans ce contexte scientifique, le.la stagiaire développera une nouvelle mesure de spectroscopie et instrumentation d’optique non linéaire, appelée microscopie par génération de second harmonique résolue en temps, afin d’enregistrer le mouvement spatio-temporel des espèces chargées, ion et électrons (ou trous), et ainsi donc cartographier les mobilités électroniques in-situ & operando le canal de l’OECT.La.le stagiaire fabriquera ces dispositifs OECTs en salle blanche de microélectronique, et bénéficiera d’un accompagnement technique pour leur réalisation. Il.elle enregistrera et analysera les FoMs clés grâce à l'expérimentation d’optique non linéaire développée et aux caractérisations électriques et électrochimiques afin d’établir, de manière plus globale, des règles d’ingénierie dans ces PMIECs qui serviront de socle de connaissances incontournables à l’avenir, pour mettre en œuvre et appliquer des circuits neuromorphiques à base d'OECTs, comme première brique d’une intelligence artificielle d’électronique organique. Pour aller plus loin :[1] https://iconic.mines-stetienne.fr/[2] https://doi.org/10.1038/ s43586-021-00065-8[3] https://www.nature.com/articles/s41578-023-00622-5🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vousLa candidate ou le candidat devra être en cours de formation et d’apprentissage d’un diplôme de Master 2 ou de 3ème année de diplôme d’ingénieurs en Techniques Optiques et Instrumentations. La candidate ou le candidat devra disposer d’une culture solide en Physique/ Science des Matériaux/ (Opto)Électronique par sa formation initiale et/ou son expérience professionnelle.Ce sujet de stage M2 Recherche a vocation d’être poursuivi en cycle de doctorat. Seul.e un.e étudiant.e intéressé.e pour continuer en doctorat sera donc retenu.e pour ce stage.  🔍 Ce que nous recherchonsLes principaux critères d’évaluation du candidat seront les suivants (liste non exhaustive) :         Maitrise technique et scientifique en Optique.
